# HarnessDock v0.1.5-rc.2

HarnessDock `v0.1.5-rc.2` aligns the sealed desktop Runtime with DeepSeek Harness `dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2` and completes the Rescue Web, first-paint, WebView compatibility, Host Protocol v2 diagnostics, configurable profile startup, and managed-process lifecycle hardening needed for the current candidate line.

This tag is a **replaceable release-candidate build**. Stable `v0.1.5` remains immutable. A reissue of this candidate is allowed only after the exact new main SHA passes all same-SHA source, mobile, packaged-startup, candidate-artifact, checksum, and Runtime identity gates.

## Runtime alignment

- Pinned upstream source: `dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2`
- Pinned upstream commit: `fb2c4b9e698e30edb738bca4cf0618587db7d203`
- Desktop candidates build the official upstream source closure and package it as a sealed local Runtime.
- Android and iOS remain Remote Gateway clients and do not embed a desktop Runtime.
- Product base version remains `0.1.5`, matching the pinned dsh base SemVer; the candidate identity is carried by the `rc.2` release tag rather than by an unrelated product-version bump.

## Rescue Web and plugin recovery

Rescue Web is now a real recovery boundary rather than a best-effort single-plugin bypass:

- Normal mode keeps the normal plugin composition and reports browser-side plugin failures with the exact attributed plugin identifier.
- Safe / Rescue Web always starts the shipped official `web` profile in a generation-private `DSH_HOME` from process birth; it never composes or heals the user's normal profile.
- Official DeepSeek Web plus HarnessDock embedded/compat/shell integrations remain available in the private Rescue Runtime.
- User patch files may be read side-effect-free for diagnostics and plugin attribution only; Rescue does not run `dsh --dump-config` against the failing user profile.
- A normal or quarantine startup that hits `atomic-write`, `profiles/node_modules.lock`, or the upstream writer-lock timeout switches directly to private Rescue instead of retrying recovery work against the same user home.
- HarnessDock does not blindly delete the user's lock file; a genuinely active writer remains untouched while Rescue restores Web availability from its private home.
- Diagnostics exposes Normal / Rescue Web / Quarantine state, isolated plugins, suspected plugins, direct Rescue Web startup, and **恢复全部插件并正常重启**.
- Restoring all plugins converts persisted `startupPolicy=safe` back to `auto` before the normal restart so repaired installations do not silently re-enter rescue mode.

## Browser diagnostics through Host Protocol v2

The temporary direct diagnostic IPC has been removed. Browser plugin failure reporting now uses the same Host Protocol v2 command path as other remote Harness actions:

- typed `report-client-plugin-failure { plugin }` command;
- HarnessWeb-only diagnostic-report capability;
- RuntimeLease, exact origin, Runtime generation, and surface checks before authorization;
- Host Kernel queue, Capability Broker, request-id dedupe, Reconciler state update, and ordered host events;
- canonical ASCII plugin-identifier validation so raw stack traces, URLs, local paths, tokens, and arbitrary error text cannot cross the WebView-to-Host diagnostic boundary.

The remote Harness surface does not receive diagnostics-admin, plugin-admin, update-install, app-quit, or other local privileged capabilities. The old `report_client_plugin_failure` Tauri command and its standalone permission are no longer part of the production IPC surface.

## WebView compatibility and first-paint handoff

- The pre-page compatibility layer provides a real `%IteratorPrototype%`-backed `Iterator` global for older WebView2 runtimes.
- PDF.js 6.x can extend `Iterator.prototype`, and built-in iterators share the extension as required.
- The official `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar-documentpreview` plugin stays enabled in normal mode; Rescue Web is not used to hide an official compatibility defect.
- The first Harness paint is covered by an in-place loading card and handed off only after meaningful Harness/error content exists for two compositor frames.
- There is no arbitrary sleep, second Harness WebView, or continuous blur/filter repaint in the first-screen handoff.

## dsh profile startup

Diagnostics exposes validated Runtime launch preferences:

- **Profile** — maps to `dsh --profile <name>`; default remains `web`.
- **DSH_HOME** — optional absolute profile/config root used by normal/direct startup; blank preserves the normal dsh environment/platform default.
- **Auto** — selected profile first; web keeps normal recovery/quarantine behavior; non-web failures fall back to Rescue Web instead of applying web-centric attribution to a different plugin tree.
- **Direct** — one selected-profile attempt with no automatic recovery masking the first error.
- **Safe / Rescue Web** — always starts the built-in `web` profile with a generation-private `DSH_HOME`; the configured/user home is not composed by the Rescue Runtime.

The setting cannot replace the bundled Node/dsh executable. The sealed Runtime `imageIdentity`, generation nonce, PID/origin validation, and `RuntimeLease` remain authoritative.

## Startup, refresh and exit lifecycle

- Runtime/Harness startup is scheduled immediately after Host Kernel setup; optional tray, updater, and native-menu initialization do not serially block the primary Web path.
- Once Harness Web is visible, refresh, Runtime restart, Rescue Web restart, and normal quit use an in-place lifecycle overlay in the already-painted primary WebView.
- A second lifecycle operation is rejected while the current Harness navigation is still loading, preventing overlapping refresh/restart watchdogs and Runtime churn.
- RuntimeActor rejects overlapping start generations and restart keeps strict stop-before-start ordering.
- Windows managed Runtime descendants remain inside `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` Job Objects; Unix managed children remain in dedicated process groups.
- Shutdown closes new-process admission first, performs strict tree cleanup off the presentation worker, observes actor/registry drain, and executes a final idempotent no-orphan pass before exit.
- Runtime work directories, including `rescue-dsh-home`, are removed when the owning Runtime generation stops.
- The Windows installed-client smoke requires a real bundled `node.exe` before normal close and then proves HarnessDock, Runtime, and bundled Node processes from the installed tree reach zero.

## Release gates preserved

This candidate does not lower or skip existing release policy. The merge/release decision remains bound to one exact SHA and includes:

- ordinary `ci` and release-contract checks;
- `tauri-ci` shared-core plus Windows/macOS/Linux Rust;
- Android APK build/package-size gate;
- iOS simulator build;
- Windows clean one-click build, exact installer install, normal Harness Web startup proof, then a second installed startup with an injected user `profiles/node_modules.lock` that must fail over to private Rescue and still reach authenticated Harness Web;
- macOS/Linux POSIX one-click Runtime/Rust gates;
- `tauri-candidate` multi-platform artifact production;
- same-SHA packaged Windows startup that repeats both the normal and profile-writer-lock Rescue scenarios;
- release asset assembly, sealed Runtime identity re-verification, and `SHA256SUMS` verification before GitHub publication.

## Upstream package note

GitHub has published `dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2`. Where the public npm umbrella package still reports an earlier prerelease, HarnessDock stays pinned to the immutable upstream Git tag/commit and builds from source; provenance does not invent an unavailable npm tarball or integrity value.
